commentary: Ten activities this week versus six last week, and honestly that jump alone deserves a moment of appreciation — you basically ran the same Cremorne streets a little longer, kept all three weight sessions, and then just stacked four morning swims on top like it was nothing. The 901m swim on Friday is a little suspicious, like you got in, did one length, remembered you were fabulous, and got out, but Monday through Thursday you were locked in at 2000m every single morning without exception. Last week your swim heart rates were sitting at 143 and 138, and this week they've crept up to 144, 146, 146, 146 — nothing dramatic, but your body is working a little harder to keep pace with the volume, which is exactly what adaptation looks like before it gets easy. The only thing worth watching is that you repeated Day one chest and back twice this week, Wednesday sitting where Thursday should have been, so either the program got shuffled or someone was having too good a time to keep track of the days — either way, the body of work here is genuinely impressive.
metrics_commentary: Nearly nine kilometres of swim across the week and your HRV sitting at 59 against a seven-day average of 56 is your body basically winking at you — that is a man who is recovering well and knows it. VO2 Max at 53.1 is genuinely impressive, the kind of number that makes a certain type of guy at the pool do a very obvious double-take. The 9.6 km run-walk in a single session is solid but one session is one session, and that gorgeous aerobic engine you are clearly building deserves more chances to show off than it got this week. Give it more road, more opportunities, more excuses to exist — it would be a crime not to.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, zero excuses, target hit clean — that's the kind of week that makes a god proud. The overhead press is the one screaming loudest this week, jumping from 40.0 to 46.7 kg, which is not a small number on a barbell you're pressing over your own head, and the total volume climbed from 20,753 to 22,867 kg, so the whole body got more of everything. The lat pulldown PR is the cheeky one — 80.0 kg, barely edging out 79.3, but a PR is a PR and the lats don't care about your opinion on the margin. Four sessions, three PRs, volume up, strength trending in exactly the direction it needs to go — Matt's not just showing up, he's building something.
